comments.story_title: Mitchell Baker Named CEO of Mozilla
comments.why_zh: 捕捉了 Mozilla 开源时代的那股激情
comments.quote_zh: 在我看来，《Code Rush》这部纪录片是必看的，能感受到那个时代的一些激情。
comments.text_zh: > 有人能说点关于她的正面评价吗？她正是 Mozilla 今天能作为一个独立的非营利组织存在的原因。1998 年 3 月 31 日，Netscape 允许 Mozilla 代码库以 Mozilla Project 的名义开源。[1][2] 这是一整年密集努力的结果：（1）移除无法开源的专有源代码，（2）以一个全新的许可证——Mozilla Public License——发布源代码。这个许可证主要由 Mitchell Baker 撰写，她的正规教育背景是法律，撰写过程中有 ESR、Linus Torvalds、VA Research 等人提供意见。[3] 2003 年 7 月 14 日，AOL（此前已收购 Netscape）关闭了 Netscape 部门，几乎裁掉了那里的所有人，包括 Mitchell Baker。就在同一天，Mitch Kapor [4] 带着资金和建议介入，帮助 Baker 和一个总共 10 名员工的核心团队，在山景城的一间办公室里成立了 Mozilla Foundation，那间办公室今天由 Khan Academy 使用。[5] 维基百科 [6] 对她的职业生涯有很好的概述。在我看来，《Code Rush》这部纪录片是必看的，能感受到那个时代的一些激情。[7][8] 能认出 JWZ 的话额外加分。:-)
comments.text: > Does anyone can tell anything positive about her? She's the reason Mozilla exists today as an independent, non-profit organization. On March 31, 1998 Netscape allowed the Mozilla code base to be open sourced under the Mozilla Project. [1][2] This was the result of an intensive year-long effort to (1) remove proprietary source code that couldn't be open-sourced, (2) release the source code under a brand new license called the Mozilla Public License. This license was written principally by Mitchell Baker whose formal education is in law, with input from ESR, Linus Torvalds, VA Research, etc. [3] On July 14, 2003 AOL (which had acquired Netscape earlier) closed down the Netscape division and laid off almost everyone there, including Mitchell Baker. That very day Mitch Kapor [4] stepped in with funding and advice to help Baker and a core team of total 10 employees set up the Mozilla Foundation in an office in Mountain View that is today occupied by the Khan Academy. [5] Wikipedia [6] has a good summary of her career. The documentary Code Rush is required viewing, IMHO, to capture some of the excitement of that era. [7][8] Bonus points for spotting JWZ. :-) [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [LINK] [4] [LINK] [5] [LINK] [6] [LINK] [7] [LINK] [8] [VIDEO]

comments.author: purerandomness
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Career and life advice for a 30yo
comments.why_zh: 传达在 Netscape 做重要事情的精神
comments.quote_zh: 我看了关于 Netscape 的纪录片《Project Code Rush》[2]，里面有 Jamie Zawinski，我很喜欢那种精神，以及做重要事情的感觉。
comments.text_zh: 有一大群人和你感受完全一样，他们聚集在所谓的“Maker communities”（创客社区）里。不错的入门入口是 IndieHackers 播客，以及像 MicroConf 这样的会议（在这里看他们的会议演讲录像，尤其是 Patrick McKenzie，也就是 patio11 [0]）。基本理念是为你自己、依赖你的人以及其他许多人，创造一份你热爱的可持续工作。这是“Our incredible journey”——也就是 VC 套现退出——的反面。一旦你做到了这一点，你就可以做任何你想做的事。开一家游戏公司。投身学术界 [1]。加入 demoscene，环游世界，参加 demo party 比赛，写出牛逼的 64k intro。投入开源，帮助 Haiku 项目。待在你本地的 hacker space 里，帮忙创建一个独立的、基于 mesh 的 ISP。我完全知道你在说什么。我看了关于 Netscape 的纪录片《Project Code Rush》[2]，里面有 Jamie Zawinski，我很喜欢那种精神，以及做重要事情的感觉。感觉这和许多人的现实形成鲜明对比——在一家有毒的 AdTech 创业公司里推 JIRA 工单。不过，我觉得这是一种幻觉。从来就没有什么“黄金时代”，人们只是忘了狗屁工作一直都存在，你只是看不到关于它们的纪录片，没人会看。对我来说，帮助我的是意识到这个世界，或者说“行业”，不欠我任何东西，我完全只能靠自己；如果我想做有意义的事，那我就得自己创造一份可持续的工作。
comments.text: There's a wide community of people feeling just like you, assembling in "Maker communities", as they call it. Good entry points are the IndieHackers podcast, and conferences like MicroConf (watch their conference talk recordings here, especially Patrick McKenzie's aka patio11 [0]) The basic idea is to create a sustainable job you love for yourself, the people that depend on you, and many others. The antithesis of "Our incredible journey", aka VC sellout. Once you've done this, you can do whatever you want. Build a game company. Pursue academia [1]. Join the demoscene, tour the world, join demo party competitions and write sick 64k intros. Commit to open source and help the Haiku project. Hang around at your local hacker space and help create an independend mesh-based ISP. I know exactly what you're talking about. I watched the Netscape documentary "Project Code Rush" [2] with Jamie Zawinski and loved the spirit and the feeling of doing something important. It feels like it's in such a stark contrast to many people's reality, pushing JIRA tickets in a toxic AdTech startup. However, I think it's an illusion. There never was a "golden age", and people simply forget that bullshit jobs always existed, you just don't see domcumentaries of them, nobody would watch them. For me, what helped me was realizing that the world, or the "industry" doesn't owe me anything, and I'm completely on my own, and if I want to do something meaningful, well, I'll have to create my own sustainable job

comments.text_zh:
结合上下文和你提到的 Quake，我猜你说的“older days”是指 90 年代、PC 和早期的 Windows？如果你之前不知道 “The Old New Thing” 这个博客，Raymond Chen 到现在已经分享了几十年关于 Windows 95 开发的故事了。多到什么程度呢，他以同名出版了一本书（这本书基本上就是博客精选集的纸质版）。os2museum[1] 博客也是一座金矿。Tim Paterson 曾经尝试开始写博客，分享了一些关于 DOS 早期的轶事[2]。说到书，你可能会喜欢讲 NT 开发过程的《Showstopper!》，虽然它在技术方面有点浅。技术方面的话，你可以把它和 Helen Custer 的《Inside Windows NT》（第一版）一起看。你可能还会喜欢：“Another Boring Topic”[3] YouTube 频道，事无巨细地（其中也包括）讲早期 Windows 开发，以及 “Old Computers Sucked”[4]，它真的会尝试在同时代的硬件上运行那些软件。“Cathode Ray Dude” 内容很杂，但也经常涉及那个年代前后的硬件和软件[5]。已经有相邻的评论提到了 JWZ 的博客，如果你对 Netscape 有美好的回忆，你可能会喜欢 “Project Code Rush”[6]。顺便说一句，Netscape Navigator 3.0 刚刚满 30 岁了。

[1] [LINK] [2] [LINK] [3] [LINK] [4] [LINK] [5] [LINK] [6] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Given the context and your reference to Quake, I assume by "the older days" you mean the 90s, PCs and early Windows? If you weren't previously aware of "The Old New Thing" blog, Raymond Chen has been sharing stories about Windows 95 development for decades at this point. So many in fact, he published a book under the same name (the book is essentially a best-of collection from the blog in paper form). The os2museum[1] blog is also a gold mine. Tim Paterson at one point tried to start blogging, sharing a few anecdotes about the early days of DOS[2] Speaking of books, you might enjoy "Showstopper!" about the development of NT, even tough it is a bit shallow on the technical side. For the technical aspects, you might want to get it together with "Inside Windows NT" (first edition) by Helen Custer. You might also enjoy: "Another Boring Topic" [3] YouTube channel, covering (among other things) early Windows development in excruciating detail and "Old Computers Sucked" [4], actually trying to run the software on era appropriate hardware. "Cathode Ray Dude" is all over the place but often also covers hardware and software of roughly that era[5]. A sibling comment already mentioned JWZs blog, if you have fond memories about Netscape, you might enjoy "Project Code Rush" [6]. Btw. Netscape Navigator 3.0 has just turned 30.
